author: IGN
description:
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt's Remastered update revisted by Travis Northup on Xbox Series X & PC, also available on PlayStation 5 & Nintendo Switch.

"The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered’s greatest asset isn’t that it adds anything the original sorely lacked, but rather that it removes some of the biggest roadblocks to fun the 1.0 version was saddled with. Combat is more challenging but also easier to enjoy, movement is quicker and less irritating, and revised skill trees allow for more freedom. Even if it doesn’t manage to fix some of the technical issues (plus I’m sure there are some bugs waiting for me to encounter them that haven’t reared their ugly heads yet), it manages to make this classic RPG more enjoyable in 2026, and that’s worth yet another ride down its well-trodded roads."

#IGN #Gaming
title: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt Remastered Review Update Video

author: IGN
description:
Welcome back to Next-Gen Console Watch! This week Daemon, Ryan, and Max take a look at ex-PlayStation Worldwide Studios boss Shuhei Yoshida's recent comments about this current generation. Yoshida doesn't think gamers are interested in a PlayStation 6 or really any new generation of gaming hardware, and the PS5/Switch 2 generation should go for as long as possible. While our wallets might appreciate, can PlayStation's business model go beyond the usual 5-7 year lifespan of gaming hardware? And what about Microsoft, whose Xbox business has not been performing well in the last two generations? Maybe their mysterious Project Helix could be the thing that gives that brand a much-needed shot in the arm. Plus we have last week's poll results and a new poll for you to vote on at IGN.com, Spotify, and Discord.
Join our Discord here! https://discord.gg/uRvkrfAws
Listen or watch on Spotify https://open.spotify.com/show/7dMyUskIpdnmlVGhio5FCn?si=kYjFb8SsTBqt-EVlwWA39w
title: 8 Years Isn't Enough: Why This Console Generation Needs to Be Longer - Next-Gen Console Watch

The series follows misfit high‑schooler Carrie White (Summer H. description:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer reviewed by Luke Reilly on Xbox Series X. Also available on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S, and PC.

"Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a fabulous looking and frantically fast anti-grav racer that impressively goes further than just taking the decades-old Star Wars Racer games and giving them a 4K facelift. With a range of satisfyingly customisable vehicle classes beyond podracers, a world outside the racing you can soak in and explore in third-person, and an interesting roguelite-adjacent structure that injects a considerable degree of risk into the action, Galactic Racer is a fresh and accomplished blend of Lucas lore with the destructive spirit of arcade racing icons like Burnout and MotorStorm. title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Review

Don't miss the 'Instant Connection' Featurette for Klara and the Sun, a comedic sci-fi drama film distributed by Sony Pictures. Hear from Jenna Ortega on portraying an artificial friend in Klara and the Sun, in theaters on October 23.

Klara and the Sun introduces audiences to Klara (Jenna Ortega), an Artificial Friend who wants nothing more than to find the perfect home. When Klara meets Josie (Mia Tharia), each immediately senses a kindred spirit in the other. Josie has a fraught relationship with her mother (Amy Adams), and they’ve suffered great loss, but Klara’s innocent wonder and unwavering loyalty begin to heal the family and bring light to Josie’s complicated world.

Klara and the Sun stars Jenna Ortega, Amy Adams, Mia Tharia, Aran Murphy, Steve Buscemi, Natasha Lyonne, and more. The film is directed by Taika Waititi and executive produced by Gary Barber, Alex G. Scott, Jeffrey Clifford, Rosie Alison, and Kazuo Ishiguro.

Klara and the Sun is in theaters on October 23.
